findings.issue_text: RSS-provided HTML is stored with `raw_html` and rendered via `raw`, bypassing sanitization and enabling stored XSS on the forum origin
Redirect destinations are not revalidated after initial host validation, allowing an approved host to redirect `open-uri` requests to internal services and cause SSRF
`open(url).read` buffers responses without a size limit, allowing large responses to exhaust Sidekiq worker memory
Feed polling calls `i.content.scrub` without handling RSS items that only provide `description`, so nil content aborts the entire poll
Using separate `SETNX` and `EXPIRE` operations can leave a permanent throttle key if a worker fails between them
Protocol-relative links such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png` are incorrectly treated as root-relative and rewritten to an invalid source-host URL
Existing embeds do not update their topic titles, causing title-only feed changes to be ignored and content changes to update only the post body
`embed_url` uses a bounded string column without input-length validation, causing overlong valid URLs to fail during import and remain stuck on the loading page
Removing the documented `--category`/`-c` option breaks existing Disqus import commands and prevents topics from being imported into the requested category
The Disqus batch importer performs an unrescued network fetch for every thread, so one unavailable or malformed source URL aborts the remaining import
Embed message origin authorization uses substring matching instead of exact parsed-origin comparison and does not verify `e.source`, allowing messages from a distinct origin to be accepted

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS-provided HTML is stored with `raw_html` and rendered via `raw`, bypassing sanitization and enabling stored XSS on the forum origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a security vulnerability. In poll_feed.rb, RSS content is imported via `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` where content comes from `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. In topic_embed.rb, posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In post.rb, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any sanitization. In best.html.erb, the content is rendered with `raw post.cooked`, which outputs HTML without escaping. This chain allows arbitrary HTML/JavaScript from RSS feeds to be stored and rendered, creating a stored XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redirect destinations are not revalidated after initial host validation, allowing an approved host to redirect `open-uri` requests to internal services and cause SSRF

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in `topic_embed.rb` line 47-50 that `open(url)` is called with user-controlled URLs after only validating the initial host. In `topic_retriever.rb` the `invalid_host?` check validates `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` but this only checks the initial URL. When `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read`, Ruby's open-uri follows HTTP redirects by default. An attacker could set up an approved host that redirects to internal services (e.g., http://localhost, http://169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata). The code doesn't validate redirect destinations, creating an SSRF vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `open(url).read` buffers responses without a size limit, allowing large responses to exhaust Sidekiq worker memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 27: `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 47: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`. Both use `open(url)` or `open(url).read` without any size limits. This is a real security/reliability issue - a malicious or misconfigured feed URL could return an extremely large response that would be fully buffered into memory, potentially exhausting Sidekiq worker memory. This is a verifiable defect in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Using separate `SETNX` and `EXPIRE` operations can leave a permanent throttle key if a worker fails between them

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 24-29, the code uses separate $redis.setnx and $redis.expire calls. If the process crashes or is killed between these two operations, the key will be set without an expiration, causing a permanent throttle that would prevent the embed URL from ever being retrieved again. This is a real race condition bug. The fix would be to use a single atomic operation like SET with EX/NX options.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Protocol-relative links such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png` are incorrectly treated as root-relative and rewritten to an invalid source-host URL

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the `absolutize_urls` method in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`. The code checks `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` to detect relative URLs. However, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/image.png` also start with `/`, so they would be incorrectly matched and rewritten to something like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/image.png`, which is invalid. The code should check for `start_with?('/')` but NOT `start_with?('//')` to properly handle protocol-relative URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing embeds do not update their topic titles, causing title-only feed changes to be ignored and content changes to update only the post body

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the TopicEmbed.import method in app/models/topic_embed.rb, when an embed already exists (the else branch starting around line 30), the code only updates the post content via PostRevisor.revise! and updates the content_sha1. However, it never updates the topic title. The title parameter is passed to the method but is only used when creating a new topic (in the PostCreator.new call). For existing embeds, if the title changes in the source feed but content stays the same, nothing happens. If content changes, only the post body is updated, not the topic title. This is a real bug where title updates from feeds are silently ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed_url` uses a bounded string column without input-length validation, causing overlong valid URLs to fail during import and remain stuck on the loading page

adjudication.rationale: The migration in db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb creates embed_url as a string column without specifying a length limit. In Rails with most databases, this defaults to VARCHAR(255). The TopicEmbed model validates presence of embed_url but has no length validation. URLs can legitimately exceed 255 characters, and when TopicEmbed.import() is called with such a URL, the database insert will fail. The embed controller would then keep showing the loading page since no TopicEmbed record exists. This is a real bug where valid long URLs would fail silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the documented `--category`/`-c` option breaks existing Disqus import commands and prevents topics from being imported into the requested category

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows in lib/tasks/disqus.thor that the method_option for 'category' (line 117) is removed, and the code that used it (lines 144-147 setting category_id based on options[:category]) is also removed. This breaks backward compatibility for users who were using the --category/-c flag in their Disqus import commands. The option was documented and functional before this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The Disqus batch importer performs an unrescued network fetch for every thread, so one unavailable or malformed source URL aborts the remaining import

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows changes to lib/tasks/disqus.thor where TopicEmbed.import_remote is called for each thread in a loop. Looking at TopicEmbed.import_remote in app/models/topic_embed.rb, it calls open(url).read which performs a network fetch. If this fails (network error, malformed URL, etc.), it will raise an exception. Since there's no rescue block around the loop in the Disqus importer, one failed URL would abort the entire import process for remaining threads. This is a real defect in the batch import functionality.
